Messages.Author: Johan Meijdam
Messages.Body:
It's probably not a new idea, but maybe it's a good idea to simplify the
Strike:Dodge rule so it cancels opponent's strike.

This has the following benefits:
1. It can be used against steal, S:CE and similar strikes
2. It makes the game easier to explain to newbies
3. It makes the game more logical: why should it NOT be possible to
dodge a shattering blow (for instance)?

Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:



Uhm.. correct me if I'm wrong.. but doesn't Strike: Dodge already
work this way? I was under the impression that "Dodge" basically
translated to "Cancel the effect of opponent's strike.", except
that Strike: Combat Ends can not be dodged (nor things like
Scorpion Sting, but that's card-text specific).
But you can dodge Steal/Destroy Equipment strikes, surely.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Johan Meijdam wrote:
>
> It's probably not a new idea, but maybe it's a good idea to simplify the
> Strike:Dodge rule so it cancels opponent's strike.
>
> This has the following benefits:
> 1. It can be used against steal, S:CE and similar strikes

It can be used against steal and any other offensive strike.

> 2. It makes the game easier to explain to newbies

Possibly. But so would doing away with intercept, aggravated damage,
and torpor. That doesn't necessarily mean that doing so is a good idea.

Explain it this way: dodge cancels the effects of the opponent's strike
on the dodger (but not his retainers).

> 3. It makes the game more logical: why should it NOT be possible to
> dodge a shattering blow (for instance)?

You have always been able to dodge a Shattering Blow.

The "cancel opponent's strike" is not more logical when refering to
a self-destructive strike: why would dodging a grenade return the
grenade, intact and with the pin restored, to the vampire who threw
it?
